study.title: Multi-kinase inhibitors can associate with heat shock proteins through their NH2-termini by which they suppress chaperone function
study.license: Original article states Creative Commons Attribution; source and authors credited.

historical_question.original_question: Inspect direct binding/ATPase controls, exposures and normal-cell effects; retain imaging-versus-western discrepancy rather than treating all signal loss as protein depletion.
answered_components: Exact source distinguishes early epitope-dependent imaging loss from denaturing western abundance
Actual AR-12/OSU-03012 versus sildenafil pretreatment and compound-specific ATPase comparisons
Drug, biotin conjugate, docking and genetic perturbations kept distinct
Reported BubR1/BUB3/PLK4 expression null identified as data not shown
remaining_components: Original supplemental death assays/captions and exact dose-response contrasts remain unreviewed
Normal-cell selectivity remains a prior-work claim, with no direct current-paper comparator qualified
Binding affinity/site certainty and full ATPase assay specificity remain limited

central_judgment: AR-12 is an inhibitory chaperone/tumor-cell perturbation in this paper, not a stabilizer restoring BUBR1 or healthy renewal. Early epitope-dependent immunofluorescence loss is not interchangeable with protein depletion, and antibody-signal loss is not by itself proof of ATPase inhibition.

compound_identity.AR-12: The original explicitly identifies OSU-03012 as AR-12. Materials lists OSU-03012 from Selleckchem and OSU-03012/AR-12 plus AR-13 supplied by Arno Therapeutics; experiment-to-lot mapping, catalog numbers and purity are not supplied in the read Methods.
compound_identity.sildenafil: Actual sildenafil purchased from Selleckchem; source also uses Viagra as a name. Salt, catalog number, formulation and clinically equivalent exposure are not established here.
compound_identity.biotin_probe: NHS-PEG12-biotin conjugate of AR-12 is the proteomic bait; not assumed identical in binding selectivity or potency to unmodified AR-12. Authors selected a nominally nonessential region and long linker, without a side-by-side bioequivalence assay qualified here.
compound_identity.AR-13: Distinct sulfonamide analogue, not an AR-12 alias. Its lower reported ATPase IC50 and stronger combination killing are not transferred to AR-12.
compound_identity.other_agents: Sorafenib tosylate, regorafenib, pazopanib, celecoxib, afatinib and ruxolitinib are distinct source comparators; no generic kinase-inhibitor or drug-family efficacy inheritance.

experiments.models: HuH7/HT1080; GBM5/GBM12 and related GBM isolates as individually captioned, all tumor models.
experiments.exposure: Fig 1A/B AR-12 0-3 µM with or without sildenafil 2 µM for 2 h. Key GBM comparisons AR-12 2 µM with or without sildenafil 2 µM, 2 h epitope comparison and 6 h denaturing western comparison.
experiments.controls: Vehicle, each drug alone and combinations where captioned; ERK2/JNK1 signal controls; scrambled siRNA, target siRNA and CMV/overexpression controls for antibody specificity; multiple N-terminal/middle/C-terminal antibodies.
experiments.result: N-terminal HSP90/GRP78/HSP70 in situ detection falls, while middle/C-terminal signals show smaller or absent change and early denaturing western signals do not show the same loss. ERK2/JNK1 are unchanged by both methods. Alternative CHAPS or beta-cyclodextrin permeabilization reportedly did not remove the discrepancy, data not shown.
experiments.denominator: Figures 1A/B and 3C quantify 40 different cells per condition, mean ± SEM; cell-versus-independent-experiment mapping is not given for each panel. General triplicate/three-study statement does not make 40 independent biological replicates.
experiments.interpretation: Consistent with altered epitope accessibility/conformation, not direct structural proof or a universal absence of later degradation. Target-siRNA antibody validation is not validation that drug-induced fluorescence loss equals depletion.
experiments.native_scope: Captions and main text read; Fig 1-2/10-11 pixels not reviewed.

experiments.result: HSP27 shows more agreement between imaging and western in Fig 3B, but its N-terminal antibody can retain signal when other epitopes lose signal. AR-12 changes chaperone localization/co-localization and co-precipitation; HSP70/HSP40 localization is not changed in Fig 8, while mitochondrial chaperone patterns change. Early AKT T308 effect is little or absent compared with larger mTOR S2448 reduction.
experiments.limit: Do not force every chaperone or antibody into one abundance explanation. Image overlap and co-precipitation are not direct binary binding or a restored protein function. Supplemental numerical contrasts are unqualified.

experiments.model: SKBR3 tumor-cell lysate after 24 h serum-free medium.
experiments.protocol: Preclear with streptavidin beads for 30 min at 4°C; biotin-AR-12 with or without excess unlabelled AR-12 for 2 h at 4°C; streptavidin capture for another 2 h; wash, gel-band selection and tandem mass spectrometry.
experiments.controls: Bead preclearing and unlabelled-AR-12 competition select bands. Exact bait/competitor concentrations, quantitative enrichment and complete false-discovery/peptide validation not supplied in the read Methods.
experiments.result: Chaperone-associated proteins, ULK1, PLK4 and redox proteins are identified as AR-12-dependent co-capture candidates. HSP27 lacks an ATP-binding site and is explicitly treated as an indirect interactor in Discussion.
experiments.binding_limit: Co-capture may reflect complexes. No direct purified binding Kd/Ki, thermal shift, site mutant, covalent occupancy or crystal structure establishes each protein as a direct selective drug target. No proteomic database reanalysis.

experiments.preparation: Bacterial GST-tagged HSP90 N-terminal fragment on glutathione-Sepharose, equal portions.
experiments.doses: 30, 100, 300 and 1000 nM AR-12 and separate drug comparators; source Results states ATP substrate 0.1 mM.
experiments.timing: Caption: 30 min drug incubation at 37°C before ATP-lite substrate; Methods also describes a 15 min reaction at 37°C after reagent addition. Not a cellular exposure or pharmacokinetic concentration.
experiments.reported_result: AR-12 IC50 approximately 200 nM; AR-13 approximately 40 nM. Sorafenib/pazopanib inhibit; regorafenib and celecoxib have little or no comparable inhibition in this preparation. Values are source estimates, not fitted/recalculated here.
experiments.readout: ATPlite 1step luminescence reported as ATPase activity, not an orthogonal direct substrate-turnover measurement.
experiments.n: Caption n = 3 (×3), ± SEM; general Methods states triplicate experiments individually repeated three times. Preparation-level independence and curve-fit uncertainty are not detailed.
specificity_limits: No GST-only/no-enzyme or drug–luminescence interference control is reported in the examined assay Methods/caption.
No orthogonal ATP/ADP/phosphate assay, broad selectivity panel or kinetic competition series is qualified.
N-terminal fragment assay cannot establish all full-length intracellular chaperone functions.
experiments.native_scope: Original supplied JPEG Fig 13A-C actually viewed; plotted directions checked, no point digitization.

experiments.model: GBM12 transfected with HSP70-GFP or FLAG-HSP90; 24 h later vehicle or sildenafil 2 µM for 1 h, followed by tag immunoprecipitation with phosphatase inhibitors.
experiments.protocol: Equal immunoprecipitate-bead portions receive AR-12 or distinct comparator 30-1000 nM ex vivo for 30 min at 37°C before ATP-lite substrate. Sildenafil is a prior cell exposure, not described as an added purified-enzyme inhibitor in this comparison.
experiments.result: Baseline activities from sildenafil- and vehicle-pretreated cells are near identical. Sildenafil pretreatment enhances AR-12 inhibition of HSP90- and HSP70-associated ATPase. Pazopanib HSP90 inhibition is not further enhanced, although HSP70 inhibition is; regorafenib enhancement is HSP70-associated rather than HSP90-associated.
experiments.control_boundary: Complex ATPase activity can include associated proteins; not pure single-protein direct sildenafil binding.
experiments.negative_control: Afatinib/ruxolitinib 0.5-2 µM do not inhibit isolated complex ATPase in Fig 14A, yet their 1 µM each 6 h cellular combination reduces N-terminal immunofluorescence in Fig 14B. Thus antibody accessibility changes are not sufficient evidence of ATPase inhibition.
experiments.n: n = 3 (×3), ± SEM caption; Fig 14 native pixels unreviewed.

sources: Main Results describing S5, S9 and S10
experiments.measured_endpoints: Live/dead tumor-cell assay; ROS/RNS dye fluorescence; signaling and chaperone-client readouts. No muscle force, completed faithful division, tissue regeneration, current-paper animal survival or clinical outcome.
experiments.reported_positive: AR-12 and AR-13 have similar dose-dependent killing in GBM6/GBM12 as single agents; AR-13 with sildenafil is reported stronger, including >50% death at AR-13 100 nM. This is an AR-13 combination claim and is not reassigned to AR-12.
experiments.genetic_perturbations: Wild-type thioredoxin overexpression suppresses AR-12-associated oxidant signal and 48 h killing; inactive mutant increases sustained signal/killing. HSP90, GRP78 and selected paired chaperone overexpression protects tumor cells during 24 h toxic combination exposure. Dominant-negative eIF2α and other plasmids/siRNA test pathways, not administered rescue drugs.
experiments.denominator: Live/dead Methods: about 10,000 cells/well, three images per well from three separately treated wells/exposures, reported nine data points ± SEM; general study repetition is stated. Image, well and experiment units are not interchangeable.
experiments.limit: Original supplemental dose-response figures, captions, exact death percentages, normal-cell controls and quantitative pairwise statistics could not be reviewed; retain as main-text-reported results only.

experiments.exposure: AR-12 or sorafenib, with or without sildenafil; this data-not-shown statement does not independently specify cells, dose, time, antibody, denominator or test.
experiments.result: Source reports no significant alteration in PLK4, BUB3 or BubR1 expression, data not shown.
experiments.limit: No demonstrated BUBR1 stabilization, restoration, kinetochore loading, spindle-checkpoint function, chromosome segregation fidelity or BUB1B-variant rescue; do not convert a nonsignificant unshown expression result into equivalence.

safety_and_normal_cells.current_paper: No direct non-transformed-cell exposure-response comparison is established in the read original main/captions; the Discussion labels selective tumor killing as a conclusion of earlier work.
safety_and_normal_cells.related_work: Earlier normal-cell selectivity, GRP78 half-life, orthotopic survival and clinical-trial statements were not independently reread. No historical citation is converted into current-paper evidence.
safety_and_normal_cells.harms_boundary: The intended outcome in the measured tumor models is cell death with stress/autophagy and redox perturbation; this is not evidence of healthy repair. No pediatric exposure, therapeutic margin, normal-tissue renewal or MVA clinical-harm conclusion follows.

reporting_and_hierarchy.statistics: One-way ANOVA followed by two-tailed Student t tests; nominal P<0.05; experiments stated triplicate and individually repeated three times, ± SEM. Exact per-comparison P values, CIs, multiplicity correction, hierarchy/power/exclusion rules and detailed randomization/blinding are not established.
source_discrepancies: Fig 7B Results describes a 2 h treatment whereas its caption specifies 6 h; do not silently harmonize the CDC37 timepoint.
Fig 12 heading mentions HSP70 terminal antibodies, but its caption panels and Results describe c-MYC/HSPH1-p105; use panel context and do not assign it an HSP70 abundance outcome.
reporting_and_hierarchy.formal_synergy: No new Bliss/Loewe/combination-index analysis qualified; reported enhanced combination killing is not independently established additivity-model synergy.

funding_and_conflicts: Massey Cancer Center philanthropic support and Universal Inc. chair. AZ and SP are Arno Therapeutics directors; Arno holds the AR-12 license. CSC is the inventor; DW synthesized the biotin conjugate. These disclosed roles are retained without inferring misconduct.

selection_rationale.AR13_reason: AR-13 is separately administered and has a distinct Figure 13 fragment-assay result, so it merits its own bounded research-compound comparison. Missing native S5 data limits its functional claim to the main-text report rather than erasing the reported positive. Its approximately 40 nM fragment estimate and >50% death at 100 nM combination statement are not assigned to AR-12.
selection_rationale.depth_distinction: AR-13 fragment-assay evidence has native Figure 13 review; its tumor-killing evidence is main-text-only reporting of the unrecovered supplement. The entire AR-13 appraisal is not described as main-text-only.
not_automatically_admitted: Genetic thioredoxin/chaperone overexpression or siRNA constructs
selection_rationale.nonadmission_reason: These interventions remain explicit methodological or specificity context in this bounded three-identity synthesis; they are not newly proposed merely because present in an assay. No conclusion of inefficacy or permanent ineligibility follows.
